subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Space Debris: The Growing Junkyard in Orbit
description: A micro-lesson that makes Space Debris: The Growing Junkyard in Orbit usable.

hook.text: There are over 36,000 pieces of tracked debris orbiting Earth. Millions of smaller pieces are too small to track.

buildup.text: A paint fleck traveling at orbital speed packs the energy of a bullet. The ISS regularly maneuvers to dodge debris.

discovery.text: Kessler syndrome predicts a cascade: one collision creates debris causing more collisions. Orbit eventually becomes unusable.

twist.text: China's 2007 anti-satellite missile test alone created over 3,500 trackable pieces. Many will remain in orbit for centuries.

climax.text: Proposed cleanup methods include nets, harpoons, lasers, and magnetic tethers. None have been deployed at scale yet.

punchline.text: We polluted the ocean. We polluted the air. Now we're polluting orbit.

quiz.question: What is the Kessler syndrome?
options: A medical condition astronauts develop from prolonged exposure to microgravity
A cascade where debris collisions create more fragments, eventually making orbit unusable
An electromagnetic interference pattern that disables satellite communications
